schwarzer-tod#text: In the autumn of 1347 Genoese ships from the Crimea brought the plague to Messina, from where it spread within four years across Italy, France, England, Germany, and Scandinavia. The pathogen Yersinia pestis was transmitted by fleas from rats and was incurable; whole villages died out. Many looked for someone to blame and murdered Jews in numerous cities. The catastrophe led to a shortage of labor, rising wages, peasant revolts, and a new view of death and transience in art and religion.
bau-der-alhambra#title: The heyday of the Alhambra in Granada
bau-der-alhambra#summary: The Nasrid sultans build the Alhambra palace city in Granada, the most magnificent structure of Islamic Spain.
bau-der-alhambra#text: After the Christian kingdoms had conquered Córdoba and Seville in the 13th century, the Emirate of Granada remained as the last Muslim state on the Iberian Peninsula and paid tribute to Castile. On a hill above the city, the Nasrid sultans expanded the Alhambra, the red fortress, into a fortified palace city; its finest parts, such as the Comares Palace and the Court of the Lions, were built around the middle of the 14th century under Yusuf I and Muhammad V. Stucco ornament, calligraphy with verses from the Quran and with poems, colored tiles, wooden ceilings, and gardens threaded with water make the complex a high point of Islamic art. After 1492 the Spanish monarchs continued to use the Alhambra, so that it survived almost unchanged and today belongs to the World Heritage.
gruendung-von-ayutthaya#summary: King Ramathibodi I founds the city of Ayutthaya on a river island; it remains the capital of the Siamese kingdom for more than 400 years.
gruendung-von-ayutthaya#text: Ayutthaya lay on an island in the Chao Phraya river and was easily reached from the sea. From here the kings ruled large parts of present-day Thailand and in 1431 captured Angkor, the capital of the Khmer. Chinese, Persian, Japanese and European merchants settled in their own quarters, and the city became one of the most important trading centres in Southeast Asia. Theravada Buddhism shaped the court and its culture. In 1767 Burmese troops captured and destroyed the city; the new capital later became Bangkok.
osmanen-fassen-fuss-in-europa#title: The Ottomans gain a foothold in Europe
osmanen-fassen-fuss-in-europa#summary: After an earthquake Ottoman troops occupy the fortress of Gallipoli on the Dardanelles and begin the conquest of the Balkans.
osmanen-fassen-fuss-in-europa#text: In the Byzantine civil war Ottoman mercenaries had fought for Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos, who married his daughter Theodora to Orhan. When an earthquake destroyed the walls of Gallipoli in March 1354, Orhan's son Süleyman Pasha occupied the town and stayed. From this bridgehead Turkish warriors advanced into Thrace, where settlers from Anatolia made their homes. In the 1360s Adrianople fell and, as Edirne, became the new capital.
erster-hansetag#summary: The merchants and cities of the Hanseatic League meet for the first time in a joint assembly and become the trading power of the north.
erster-hansetag#text: From the 12th century onward, Low German merchants had joined together in associations in order to obtain protection and privileges abroad; trading posts in London, Bruges, Bergen, and Novgorod were their bases. In 1356 the representatives of the cities gathered for the first time in Lübeck for a Hanseatic Diet, which passed joint resolutions on trade, law, and war. At its height some 200 cities from Cologne to Reval belonged to the League, which in the Peace of Stralsund in 1370 even forced the king of Denmark into far-reaching concessions. With the rise of the Dutch and of the territorial princes, the League lost importance in the 16th century; the last Hanseatic Diet was held in 1669.
gruendung-der-ming-dynastie#summary: The rebel peasant's son Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims himself emperor in Nanjing and drives the Mongols out of China.
gruendung-der-ming-dynastie#text: Famines, floods and heavy taxation led in the 1350s to great uprisings against the Yuan, above all the Red Turban movement. Zhu Yuanzhang, who as an orphan had lived in a Buddhist monastery, prevailed over the other rebel leaders. In 1368 he proclaimed the Ming dynasty in Nanjing, his troops took Dadu, and the last Yuan emperor fled to Mongolia. As the Hongwu emperor he had the land surveyed, villages reorganized and thousands of alleged conspirators executed. The Ming ruled China until 1644.
eroberungen-timurs#summary: From Samarkand, Timur subdues Persia, India, Syria, and Anatolia and makes his capital a center of art and learning.
eroberungen-timurs#text: Timur, a Turco-Mongol warlord from what is now Uzbekistan, seized power in Samarkand in 1370 and waged war almost without interruption for the next 35 years. His mounted armies conquered Persia, defeated the Golden Horde in 1395, plundered Delhi in 1398 and Aleppo, Damascus, and Baghdad in 1400 and 1401, and in 1402 defeated the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I near Ankara, who died in captivity. As a warning Timur had towers built out of skulls; hundreds of thousands died in his campaigns, and whole regions were laid waste. At the same time he brought craftsmen, master builders, and scholars to Samarkand, where splendid mosques and mausoleums were built and where his grandson Ulugh Beg later erected one of the best observatories in the world. Timur died in 1405 at the start of a campaign against China; his descendant Babur founded the Mughal empire in India in 1526.
jikji-metalllettern-druck#title: Jikji: the oldest surviving book printed with metal type
jikji-metalllettern-druck#summary: At the Korean monastery of Heungdeoksa a collection of Buddhist teachings is printed with movable metal type, some 80 years before Gutenberg's Bible.
jikji-metalllettern-druck#text: In Korea people had already experimented with movable metal type in the 13th century. The book Jikji, a selection of teachings by Buddhist Zen masters, was printed in 1377 at Heungdeoksa monastery near Cheongju. Only the second volume survives; it is now held by the National Library of France in Paris. It is regarded as the oldest surviving book produced with movable metal type. Because Chinese requires thousands of characters, however, printing in East Asia remained mainly a matter for the state and the monasteries.
bauernaufstand-in-england#summary: Tens of thousands of peasants and craftsmen march on London under Wat Tyler and demand the end of serfdom.
bauernaufstand-in-england#text: After the Black Death, wage laborers had gained more bargaining power, but laws froze wages, and a poll tax for the war against France hit poor and rich equally hard. In June 1381 the counties of Kent and Essex rose up, marched on London under the leadership of Wat Tyler, opened prisons, and killed the Archbishop of Canterbury. The preacher John Ball asked where the nobleman had been when Adam delved and Eve span. The fourteen-year-old king Richard II promised the abolition of serfdom, but after Tyler was struck down during the negotiations the revolt was put down; serfdom nevertheless largely disappeared in England over the following decades.
schlacht-auf-dem-amselfeld#summary: On the Field of Blackbirds in Kosovo the Ottomans fight a Serbian army; both rulers are killed, and Serbia becomes a tributary of the Ottomans.
schlacht-auf-dem-amselfeld#text: On 15 June 1389 Sultan Murad I and the Serbian prince Lazar met with their armies on the Field of Blackbirds near Priština. Murad was killed during the battle by a Serbian nobleman whom tradition calls Miloš Obilić; Lazar was captured and executed. Murad's son Bayezid I took command, and Serbia soon had to pay tribute and provide troops. In Serbian memory the battle became a myth of sacrifice and loyalty that still has political effects today.
gruendung-von-joseon#title: Founding of the Joseon dynasty in Korea
gruendung-von-joseon#summary: General Yi Seong-gye overthrows the kingdom of Goryeo and founds the Joseon dynasty, which rules Korea for more than 500 years.
gruendung-von-joseon#text: Towards the end of the 14th century the kingdom of Goryeo had been weakened by attacks of Japanese pirates and by disputes over relations with the Ming. In 1388 General Yi Seong-gye turned his army back instead of marching against China and in 1392 had himself proclaimed king. He moved the capital to Hanyang, present-day Seoul. The new dynasty made Neo-Confucianism the foundation of state, family and education and pushed back the influence of Buddhist monasteries. Joseon lasted until the end of the 19th century.
aufstieg-des-sultanats-malakka#title: Rise of the Sultanate of Malacca
aufstieg-des-sultanats-malakka#summary: On the strait between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, Malacca becomes the most important hub for trade between the Indian Ocean and China.
aufstieg-des-sultanats-malakka#text: Around 1400 Parameswara, a prince from Palembang on Sumatra, founded the city of Malacca. He placed himself under the protection of the Ming and received Zheng He's fleets several times. Soon the rulers adopted Islam, and Malacca became a centre from which Islam spread across the Malay world. Merchants from Gujarat, Persia, China and Java exchanged spices, textiles and porcelain here; contemporaries reported dozens of languages being spoken in the streets. In 1511 the Portuguese conquered the city.
schlacht-bei-ankara#title: Battle of Ankara and the Ottoman Interregnum
schlacht-bei-ankara#summary: Timur defeats and captures Sultan Bayezid I; for a decade the Ottoman Empire falls apart in a war between brothers.
schlacht-bei-ankara#text: On 28 July 1402 Sultan Bayezid I, called "the Thunderbolt" because of his rapid campaigns, faced Timur's army near Ankara. Tatar horsemen and troops of Anatolian princes defected to Timur, and Bayezid was taken prisoner; he died in captivity in 1403. Timur reinstated the Anatolian princes whom the Ottomans had subjugated. Until 1413 Bayezid's sons fought over the succession, until Mehmed I reunited the empire. The crisis gave Byzantium half a century's reprieve.
fahrten-des-zheng-he#summary: On behalf of the Ming emperors, Admiral Zheng He leads seven huge fleets through Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean as far as Arabia and East Africa.
fahrten-des-zheng-he#text: In 1405 the Yongle emperor sent out a fleet of dozens of enormous treasure ships and numerous escort vessels with almost 28,000 men under the eunuch Zheng He. On seven voyages the ships visited Java, Malacca, Ceylon, Calicut, Hormuz, the Arabian Peninsula and the coast of East Africa. They brought gifts, called for tribute missions and returned with gems, spices and even giraffes. After 1433 the court ended the costly voyages and turned to the defence of the northern frontier. The fleets show that China was then building the largest ocean-going ships in the world.
bau-der-verbotenen-stadt#title: Building of the Forbidden City in Beijing
bau-der-verbotenen-stadt#summary: The Yongle emperor has a vast palace complex built in Beijing and moves the Ming capital from Nanjing to the north.
bau-der-verbotenen-stadt#text: As a prince, Yongle had resided in Beijing, and he wanted to move the capital closer to the northern frontier threatened by the Mongols. From 1406 hundreds of thousands of craftsmen and labourers worked on a palace complex with hundreds of buildings surrounded by walls and moats. The complex was finished in 1420, and in 1421 Beijing officially became the capital. It was called the Forbidden City because ordinary people were not allowed to enter it. Until 1912, 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing lived here; today it is a museum.
sternwarte-ulugh-begs#title: Ulugh Beg builds the Samarkand observatory
sternwarte-ulugh-begs#summary: Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg builds a great observatory in Samarkand whose star catalogue is among the most accurate of the pre-telescopic era.
sternwarte-ulugh-begs#text: Ulugh Beg governed Samarkand on behalf of his father and was more interested in mathematics and astronomy than in war. In the 1420s he had a three-storey observatory built on a hill, with a huge measuring arc set into the rock. His astronomers determined the positions of about 1,000 stars and the length of the year with great accuracy. In 1449 Ulugh Beg was murdered at the instigation of his own son. His tables were later translated and used in Europe as well.
aztekischer-dreibund#summary: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan join forces and found the Aztec empire.
aztekischer-dreibund#text: For a long time the Mexica of Tenochtitlan had to pay tribute to the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco. In 1428 their ruler Itzcoatl, together with Nezahualcoyotl of Texcoco and the city of Tlacopan, defeated the Tepanecs. The three cities formed an alliance, subjugated large parts of Mexico in the following decades and shared the tribute. Over time Tenochtitlan became the leading power. Around 1500 hundreds of cities from the Gulf coast to the Pacific paid levies to the Triple Alliance.
le-loi-befreit-dai-viet#title: Lê Lợi frees Đại Việt from Ming rule
le-loi-befreit-dai-viet#summary: After ten years of rebellion, Lê Lợi drives the Chinese occupiers out of Vietnam and founds the Lê dynasty.
le-loi-befreit-dai-viet#text: In 1407 the Ming had conquered the Vietnamese state of Đại Việt and tried to turn it into a Chinese province. From 1418 the landowner Lê Lợi led an uprising that began with raids from the mountains and finally defeated the Ming armies. In 1427 the Chinese withdrew, and in 1428 Lê Lợi ascended the throne as emperor. His adviser Nguyễn Trãi wrote a famous proclamation on the victory. Under the Lê dynasty Đại Việt later expanded southwards at the expense of the kingdom of Champa.
gruendung-des-mutapa-reiches#summary: After the decline of Great Zimbabwe, Shona rulers establish the empire of Mutapa in the north of the plateau.
gruendung-des-mutapa-reiches#text: According to tradition, the Shona prince Nyatsimba Mutota moved around 1430 from the region of Great Zimbabwe northwards to the Zambezi and subjugated numerous groups there. His successors bore the title Mwene Mutapa and controlled the gold and ivory trade with the Swahili merchants on the coast. In the 16th century the Portuguese pushed up the Zambezi to gain access to the gold mines. In 1629 a Mutapa ruler was forced to sign a treaty that made him dependent on Portugal. Nevertheless the empire survived in reduced form into the 19th century.
ende-angkors-als-khmer-hauptstadt#title: End of Angkor as the Khmer capital
ende-angkors-als-khmer-hauptstadt#summar: After an attack from Ayutthaya, the Khmer kings abandon their old capital of Angkor and move their seat to the south.
ende-angkors-als-khmer-hauptstadt#text: From the 9th to the 13th century the Khmer empire had dominated large parts of Southeast Asia. In the 14th and 15th centuries it came under growing pressure from the kingdom of Ayutthaya, whose troops, according to tradition, captured Angkor in 1431. The kings then moved their seat to the area of present-day Phnom Penh, closer to the trade routes on the Mekong. Researchers cite the decay of the irrigation system and droughts as further causes. Angkor Wat, however, remained an important Buddhist pilgrimage site.
brunelleschis-kuppel#title: Brunelleschi completes the dome of Florence Cathedral
brunelleschis-kuppel#summary: Filippo Brunelleschi completes the huge dome of Santa Maria del Fiore, the emblem of the early Renaissance.
brunelleschis-kuppel#text: Work on the cathedral of Florence had been going on since 1296, but no one knew how the opening, more than 40 meters wide, could be vaulted over. In 1420 Brunelleschi designed a double-shelled dome that was built without wooden centering, and for it he invented hoisting machines and a herringbone pattern of brickwork. On 25 March 1436 Pope Eugene IV consecrated the cathedral; the dome remained the largest masonry dome in the world into the 20th century and proved that the builders of the present could surpass antiquity.
pachacutec-und-das-inka-reich#title: Pachacuti builds up the Inca empire
pachacutec-und-das-inka-reich#summary: An Inca ruler turns the small kingdom of Cusco into a great empire that soon stretches across the whole of the Andes.
pachacutec-und-das-inka-reich#text: Around 1438 the prince Cusi Yupanqui repelled an attack by the Chanka on Cusco, dethroned his father, and took the name Pachacuti, he who overturns the world. In a good three decades he subdued the peoples of the highlands, had Cusco laid out anew as the capital, and introduced storehouses, labor service, and administration by means of knotted cords, the quipus. The mountain city of Machu Picchu was probably built under him as well. His successors extended the empire of the four parts, Tawantinsuyu, from Ecuador to Chile; with around ten million inhabitants it was the largest empire in the Americas when the Spaniards arrived in 1532.
oba-ewuare-erneuert-benin#title: Oba Ewuare renews the kingdom of Benin
oba-ewuare-erneuert-benin#summary: Under Oba Ewuare, Benin becomes a powerful kingdom with a fortified capital and a famous court art.
oba-ewuare-erneuert-benin#text: Ewuare, known as the Great, came to power around 1440 as oba, or king, of Benin in what is now southern Nigeria. He rebuilt the capital with broad streets and a vast system of earthen walls and moats and expanded the kingdom through military campaigns. At court, guilds of casters and carvers made commemorative heads, relief plaques and ivory works for the ancestral altars of the kings. From the 1480s Benin traded with Portuguese merchants. The works known as the Benin Bronzes were looted by British troops in 1897; their return is still being negotiated today.
koenig-sejong-verkuendet-hangeul#title: King Sejong promulgates the Hangeul script
koenig-sejong-verkuendet-hangeul#summary: The Korean king Sejong publishes a new, easy-to-learn alphabet so that ordinary people too can read and write.
koenig-sejong-verkuendet-hangeul#text: Until then Koreans wrote with Chinese characters, which only a small educated elite had mastered. In 1443 King Sejong had a script developed with originally 28 letters, some of whose shapes depict the position of the speech organs. In 1446 it was promulgated under the title Hunminjeongeum, the correct sounds for the instruction of the people. Many scholars rejected the script as a threat to Chinese learning. Hangeul only fully prevailed in the 20th century; today South Korea celebrates Hangeul Day every year.
bau-von-machu-picchu#summary: High above the Urubamba Valley a royal estate of the Inca is built.
bau-von-machu-picchu#text: Machu Picchu lies on a mountain saddle at about 2,400 meters above sea level, some 450 meters above the Urubamba valley. The complex was probably built as an estate for Pachacuti; new radiocarbon dates show that it was already inhabited in the 1420s. Temples, houses and terraces are built of precisely fitted stones, and a canal supplied the inhabitants with spring water. The Spaniards never found the site. In 1911 the American Hiram Bingham made it known worldwide; since 1983 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
haudenosaunee-bund#summary: Five peoples in northeastern North America unite under the Great Law of Peace.
haudenosaunee-bund#text: According to tradition, the Peacemaker Deganawida and his companion Hiawatha ended the blood feuds between the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca in today's state of New York. The five peoples agreed on the Great Law of Peace and a joint council at Onondaga, which made decisions by consensus. The clan mothers chose the council members and could also remove them. When the confederacy arose is disputed; suggestions range from the 12th to the 16th century. In the 18th century the Tuscarora joined as the sixth nation.
gutenbergs-buchdruck#title: Gutenberg invents printing with movable type
gutenbergs-buchdruck#summary: In Mainz, Johannes Gutenberg develops a printing process using movable metal type and a printing press.
gutenbergs-buchdruck#text: Gutenberg combined cast individual letters made of a lead alloy, a printing press modeled on the wine press, and an oil-based printing ink. Around 1454 he completed the forty-two-line Bible, the first great printed book of Europe. Within fifty years printing shops had been set up in more than 250 European cities, and books became affordable for many people.
fall-konstantinopels#summary: The Ottomans under Mehmed II capture the Byzantine capital and bring the Eastern Roman Empire to an end.
fall-konstantinopels#text: After almost two months of siege, Ottoman troops broke through the walls of Constantinople on 29 May 1453 with the help of enormous cannon; the last emperor, Constantine XI, fell in the fighting. Sultan Mehmed II made the city, under the name Istanbul, the capital of his empire and had the Hagia Sophia converted into a mosque. Many regard the event as the end of the Middle Ages: Greek scholars fled to Italy and fostered the Renaissance there, and the search for new trade routes to Asia accelerated the European voyages of exploration.
bau-des-topkapi-palastes#summary: Mehmed II has a new palace built at the tip of Istanbul's old city, which remains the seat of government of the sultans for almost 400 years.
bau-des-topkapi-palastes#text: A few years after the conquest of Constantinople, Mehmed II began building a new palace around 1459 on the hill above the Bosporus and the Golden Horn. The Topkapı Palace was a sequence of courtyards: in the outer area the Divan, the imperial council, met, while the inner area housed the palace school, where young pages were trained as officers and officials. The harem housed the sultan's family. Only in 1856 did the court move to the Dolmabahçe Palace; since 1924 Topkapı has been a museum.
qhapaq-nan-strassennetz-der-inka#title: Qhapaq Ñan: the road network of the Inca
qhapaq-nan-strassennetz-der-inka#summary: A road system of over 30,000 kilometers links the Inca empire from Ecuador to Chile.
qhapaq-nan-strassennetz-der-inka#text: The Inca improved older paths and linked them into a network with two main routes, one through the highlands and one along the coast. Stairways, causeways and suspension bridges of woven grass crossed gorges and swamps. At regular intervals there were way stations and storehouses, the tambos. Relay runners, the chasquis, carried messages and quipus over hundreds of kilometers in a few days. The roads served the army, the administration and labor service; since 2014 they have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site in six countries.
muhammad-rumfa-reformiert-kano#title: Muhammad Rumfa reforms the Hausa state of Kano
muhammad-rumfa-reformiert-kano#summary: The ruler of Kano develops his city into the leading center of trade and learning among the Hausa states.
muhammad-rumfa-reformiert-kano#text: The Hausa states in the north of present-day Nigeria were independent city-states such as Kano, Katsina and Zaria that lived from crafts, agriculture and long-distance trade. Muhammad Rumfa, who according to the Kano Chronicle ruled from about 1463 to 1499, extended the city walls, founded the great Kurmi market and had a new palace built. He brought Muslim scholars to his court, among them the North African jurist al-Maghili, who wrote a treatise for him on the obligations of princes. Kano became famous for its indigo-dyed cotton cloth and leather goods. For centuries the city remained one of the most important markets in West Africa.
sunni-ali-erobert-timbuktu#summary: The ruler of Songhai wrests Timbuktu from the Tuareg and makes Songhai the new great power on the Niger.
sunni-ali-erobert-timbuktu#text: Songhai, with its capital Gao, had long been dependent on Mali until it turned conqueror in the 15th century under Sunni Ali. In 1468 he took Timbuktu, which had been under Tuareg control since 1433, and dealt harshly with some of its scholars. A few years later, after a long siege, he also conquered the trading city of Djenné. With a fleet of boats on the Niger and strong cavalry he created the largest empire West Africa had yet seen. After his death in 1492, Askia Mohammed seized power.
tupac-yupanqui-erobert-chimu#title: The Inca conquer the Chimú kingdom
tupac-yupanqui-erobert-chimu#summary: Under Tupac Yupanqui the Inca subjugate their greatest rival on the coast of Peru.
tupac-yupanqui-erobert-chimu#text: While his father Pachacuti was still alive, Tupac Yupanqui led the Inca armies northward. Around 1470 he subjugated the rich kingdom of Chimor on the north coast, probably in part by threatening the water supply of its valleys. The Chimú king was taken to Cusco, as were many gold- and silversmiths, whose art adorned the Inca court. With the victory over Chimor the Inca controlled the entire coast of Peru. As ruler, Tupac Yupanqui then extended the empire into Ecuador and deep into Chile.
taufe-von-nzinga-a-nkuwu#title: The king of Kongo is baptized
taufe-von-nzinga-a-nkuwu#summary: King Nzinga a Nkuwu receives baptism in his capital and seeks an alliance with Portugal.
taufe-von-nzinga-a-nkuwu#text: In 1483 the Portuguese navigator Diogo Cão had reached the mouth of the Congo River and made contact with the kingdom of Kongo, a large, well-organized state in present-day Angola and Congo. Envoys travelled to Lisbon, and in 1491 priests, craftsmen and soldiers arrived in the capital Mbanza Kongo. King Nzinga a Nkuwu was baptized there and took the name João I. He hoped the alliance would bring him prestige, weapons and knowledge. Later he partly turned away from Christianity again, but his son Afonso made it the state religion.
fall-granadas#summary: The last emir of Granada hands the city over to Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon; Muslim rule in Spain ends after almost 800 years.
fall-granadas#text: From 1482 the Catholic Monarchs Isabella and Ferdinand waged war against the Emirate of Granada, weakened by family strife, and took city after city. After a siege lasting months, Emir Muhammad XII, whom the Spaniards called Boabdil, handed over the Alhambra on 2 January 1492; according to legend he wept at his last sight of the city. The treaty of surrender guaranteed the Muslims freedom of religion and their property, yet as early as around 1500 they were forced to be baptized, and from 1609 to 1614 Spain expelled the descendants of these Moriscos. In that same year, 1492, the Jews had to leave Spain, and Columbus sailed west on the monarchs' commission. With Granada the Reconquista came to an end, the reconquest of the peninsula by the Christian kingdoms, which had begun in 711 with the Arab conquest.
kolumbus-erreicht-amerika#summary: In search of a sea route to India, Christopher Columbus lands on an island in the Bahamas on 12 October 1492.
kolumbus-erreicht-amerika#text: With three ships Columbus had sailed west from Palos on the commission of the Spanish crown, because he believed the earth to be smaller than it is. Until his death he believed that he had reached the east coast of Asia. In fact his landing began the lasting contact between Europe and America, which fundamentally changed the history of both continents.
askia-mohammed-songhai#title: Askia Mohammed takes power in the Songhai empire
askia-mohammed-songhai#summary: With Askia Mohammed begins the golden age of the Songhai empire, the largest state in West Africa, with Timbuktu as a center of scholarship.
askia-mohammed-songhai#text: After the death of the conqueror Sunni Ali, the general Mohammed Ture overthrew his son and took the ruler's title of Askia. He reorganized the empire on the Niger with provinces, officials, and a professional army, made the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1496, and promoted Islam as a unifying religion. Timbuktu with its Sankoré Mosque, and Djenné, became centers of Islamic scholarship whose manuscripts survive to this day. Trade in gold, salt, and slaves across the Sahara made Songhai one of the richest powers of the age; in 1591 it was shattered by Moroccan troops with firearms.
vertrag-von-tordesillas#summary: Spain and Portugal divide the newly discovered lands of the world, and those still to be discovered, between them along a line in the Atlantic.
vertrag-von-tordesillas#text: After the return of Columbus, the two sea powers quarreled over the rights to the new lands, and in 1493 Pope Alexander VI proposed a dividing line. In the treaty of 7 June 1494 it was fixed 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands: everything west of it was to belong to Spain, everything east of it to Portugal. Brazil, reached in 1500, thus fell to Portugal, which is still evident today in the language of the country. Other powers such as England and France never recognized the division; the treaty shows how matter-of-factly European rulers disposed of foreign continents.
vasco-da-gama-erreicht-indien#summary: The Portuguese Vasco da Gama sails around Africa and is the first European to reach India by sea.
vasco-da-gama-erreicht-indien#text: After a voyage of almost a year around the Cape of Good Hope, da Gama landed at Calicut on the Malabar Coast of India in May 1498. The new sea route bypassed the Arab and Venetian middlemen and made Portugal the leading power in the spice trade for a century. Portuguese bases were soon established from East Africa as far as China and Japan.
cabral-erreicht-brasilien#summary: A Portuguese fleet on its way to India lands on the coast of Brazil and takes possession of the land for Portugal.
